### 5. Working with Gen AI on a Bigger Problem (Optional)

Let's practice using a Gen AI tool (e.g., ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Copilot) as a coding partner on a bigger data wrangling problem, using the ideas from this week's lesson. Do part (a) on your own before you open an AI tool, and don't paste your data files into one. Share the structure of the data (like the output of `glimpse()`) instead.

A collaborator sends you this message:

> Kangaroo rats (genus *Dipodomys*) are some of the largest seed-eating rodents at Portal. The Long-term Krat Exclosure plots are fenced to keep them out while letting smaller rodents in. I'd like to know whether the *other* rodents are caught more often on those plots than on the Control plots.
>
> Using the Portal `surveys`, `species`, and `plots` data, could you send me a table (one row per year, one column per plot type) and a line plot of the number of rodents captured per plot? Please leave out all kangaroo rats, including any that were not identified to species. The two treatments don't have the same number of plots, so make sure the numbers are comparable. Also, some records have impossible dates (like April 31). Please leave those out and tell me how many records in the full `surveys` table have them.

Use the `surveys`, `species`, and `plots` data frames from Question 2 and take a look at each one with `glimpse()`. You will want this information for your prompt.


b.  Write the prompt you give the Gen AI tool and paste it below. A good prompt includes the language and packages you are using, the structure of your data (and anything only you know, like units), what you want the result to look like, any constraints (like only using functions from class), and your plan from (a).

c.  Paste the code you ended up with (after any follow-up prompts) into the code chunk below, with comments in your own words explaining each step. Make sure you can explain every line, and look up any functions you don't recognize. Save the long-format summary as `krat_summary` (with the columns `year`, `plot_type`, `total_captures`, `n_plots`, and `captures_per_plot`) and the table your collaborator asked for as `krat_table`. Then make the plot, report how many records have impossible dates, and write one sentence about what the plot shows.

d.  Gen AI can write code that runs without errors but doesn't do what you asked. Write code for at least three checks of its work, including one row-count check (e.g., rows before and after the joins and filters) and one spot check (calculate one value in `krat_table` a different way), and write a sentence about what each shows. Some other ideas: Are any kangaroo rats left? Are there any `NA`s or missing years? Does the plot look right?

e.  Reflect in 3--5 sentences. What did the AI get right? What did it get wrong or miss? (If you didn't find any problems, what did you check, and how do you know the code is right?) What would you do differently next time? End with a one-line statement like *I used \[tool name\] on \[date\] to \[what you used it for\].*
